models.name: Dry-basis feedstock and product mass balance
models.source: Felder, Rousseau & Bullard, Elementary Principles of Chemical Processes, 4th ed., Wiley (2016), material balances.
models.status: Conservation identity; implementation tested. Product split values come from the ML-001 predictor or user inputs.

models.name: Feed heating and water evaporation duty
models.source: NIST Chemistry WebBook, SRD 69, Water thermochemistry and phase-change data; Chase (1998), NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables.
models.status: Screening heat-duty balance. CoolProp/IAPWS-95 is used when available; otherwise constant-cp fallback. Global heating efficiency and heat-loss fraction are simplified assumptions.

models.name: Biomass pyrolysis product distribution
models.source: Di Blasi, C. (2008). Modeling chemical and physical processes of wood and biomass pyrolysis. Progress in Energy and Combustion Science, 34(1), 47–90. DOI: 10.1016/j.pecs.2006.12.001.
models.status: Literature-informed model structure; numerical product fractions are scenario inputs and must be validated for the feedstock/reactor.

models.name: Capital recovery factor and discounted cash flow
models.source: Peters, Timmerhaus & West, Plant Design and Economics for Chemical Engineers, 5th ed., McGraw-Hill (2003).
models.status: Standard financial mathematics; all project-specific financial inputs are user-supplied assumptions.

models.name: Scenario Pareto screening
models.source: Deb, K. (2001). Multi-Objective Optimization Using Evolutionary Algorithms. Wiley.
models.status: Deterministic comparison of candidate scenarios; optimality is limited to the scenarios supplied.

models.name: Data-driven char property predictor
models.source: Breiman, L. (2001). Random Forests. Machine Learning 45, 5-32. DOI: 10.1023/A:1010933404324.
models.status: Five-fold publication-grouped CV against a feedstock-class mean baseline. Inference selects the class mean for any target where it beats the random forest; tree spread is not a calibrated interval. Lab/pilot literature data only; not reactor-specific.

models.name: Char carbon permanence from H/C (screening)
models.source: Shape follows the common H/Corg quality classes (0.4 / 0.7; 0.7 is the EBC/IBI limit). Numeric values are placeholders, not a published regression.
models.status: PLACEHOLDER VALUES. Replace with a published BC+100 regression before any quantitative claim.

models.name: Predicted-yield process design and grid optimisation
models.source: Deb, K. (2001) for Pareto dominance; grid enumeration (no stochastic optimiser).
models.status: Optimal only within the grid and the predictor's validity range. Liquid/gas split, costs and carbon price are assumptions.

models.name: CDR pathway comparison
models.status: DACCS and enhanced weathering re-verified; biochar, BECCS and A/R figures recalled and flagged for re-check.

models.name: Particle heat transfer (1-D spherical conduction, finite volume)
models.source: Verified in code against the analytical sphere solution (Carslaw & Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids, 2nd ed., 1959).
models.status: Verified (solves its equations correctly: <0.1% vs analytical). Not validated against measured particle temperatures; property values and h are assumptions; single particle, no bed effects.

models.name: One-step global devolatilisation kinetics
models.source: Di Blasi, C. and Branca, C. (2001). Kinetics of primary product formation from wood pyrolysis. Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 40(23), 5547-5556. DOI: 10.1021/ie000997e.
models.status: Single global first-order devolatilisation step. Beech-wood parameters fitted over 573–708 K; other feedstocks and temperatures outside this range are extrapolations. Used for conversion time only, not product yields.
